# Sources: how to sharpen a kitchen knife (topic discovery)

Five sources were read (S1-S5). S6-S14 were seen only in search summaries: they are leads, and nothing rests on them alone.

### S1. Science of Sharp (blog; signs as "scienceofsharp", commenters address the author as Todd), "Seven Misconceptions About Knife Burrs", scienceofsharp.com, 2024-02-03
- Primary: the author's own experiments, imaged with a scanning electron microscope and cross-sectioned with a focused ion beam (he says so in his comment replies). Self-published, not peer-reviewed. The page states no credentials. I judged expertise from the methods and the detail, not from a CV (the site's about page was not opened). A post with the same title dated 2022-06-10 exists (snippet only); this is the newer version. URL: https://scienceofsharp.com/2024/02/03/seven-misconceptions-about-knife-burrs/
- Access: read (body text, figure captions and the author's comment replies; the micrographs did not render, so I saw the captions, not the images)
- Supports: C01, C12, C13, C15, C17, C18, C19. Counterevidence: popular guides say the burr must be removed (S12). This post finds that light strokes and stropping mostly refine and align a burr, and that a thin, undamaged burr can be "surprisingly strong" (C18 disputed). Its own hedges are kept: "I would estimate", the fingertip-feel threshold is "in my experience", and a 2025 post on the same site (S14, snippet) calls the conditions of burr formation poorly understood. The examples use a Victorinox knife, a DMT Fine plate and an Atoma 400 diamond plate, so they are not all kitchen-knife cases. The 2022 version's line that raising a burr is "a simple and largely effective technique" was seen only as a snippet.
- Status: primary observations by one experimenter. This is the best micrograph evidence on whetstone burrs that I found; the search turned up no peer-reviewed study of it.

### S2. Science of Sharp, "What Does Steeling Do? Part 1", scienceofsharp.com, 2018-08-22
- Primary: the author's own SEM images and focused-ion-beam cross-sections of edges before and after steeling with ribbed, smooth and ceramic rods. The blades are Olfa carbon-steel utility blades and one S30V knife, not kitchen knives. Self-published, not peer-reviewed, by the same author as S1 (so S1 and S2 are not independent of each other). URL: https://scienceofsharp.com/2018/08/22/what-does-steeling-do-part-1
- Access: read (text, captions and the author's comment replies; the micrographs did not render)
- Supports: C02, C21, C23. Counterevidence: the maker (S3) says honing "realigns the microscopic teeth on the edge". S8 (snippet) says a smooth steel burnishes without removing metal. Limits are stated or visible: a few specimens, only the ribbed rod was tried on a rolled edge, the conclusion is hedged with "primarily", and the later parts of the series were partly abandoned ("There hasn't been enough interest", author comment, March 2019).
- Status: primary observations, small sample. I found no newer work that replaces it.

### S3. WÜSTHOF, "How to: Sharpen Your WÜSTHOF Knives", wusthof.com, undated (page footer: © 2026)
- Primary for the maker's own angles and method. WÜSTHOF is a German knife manufacturer with a commercial interest: it sells steels, stones and sharpeners. URL: https://wusthof.com/pages/how-to-sharpen-your-wusthof-knives
- Access: read (the whole article; the illustrations had no alt text and the embedded videos were not seen)
- Supports: C01, C05, C07, C08, C09, C21, C22, C23, C25. Counterevidence: its account that honing "realigns" the edge is contradicted by S2's cross-sections (C23 disputed). Its 14 degrees for standard Western knives differs from S4's 20-25 degrees per side (C09 disputed). The page never says "per side": its procedure (hold 14 degrees, then repeat on the other side) implies it, and the maker's FAQ (S6, snippet) says it outright. Some product pages give 14.5 (snippet). The page's Thanksgiving and Black Friday banners are retail promotions, not content, and are not used.
- Status: primary record for WÜSTHOF's own knives only; it is not a general standard.

### S4. Chef Knives To Go, "How to Sharpen a Knife on a Whetstone", chefknivestogo.com, undated
- Popular practitioner guide from a specialist knife and stone retailer (family-owned since 2001; no individual author named). It has a commercial interest: it links to the stones and strops it sells. URL: https://www.chefknivestogo.com/how-to-sharpen-a-knife-on-a-whetstone.html
- Access: read (the whole article; it has no video content and the body does not discuss honing)
- Supports: C01, C05, C06, C08, C09, C10, C11, C13, C14, C16, C19, C20. Counterevidence: its Western angle (20-25 degrees per side) differs from the makers' 14-15 (S3, S7). Its coin rule of thumb ("two stacked coins give about 15 degrees on most kitchen knives") does not fit a tall chef's knife by simple geometry, so it is not used (see notes.md). On method it agrees with the popular guides seen in summaries (S12).
- Status: secondary practitioner account. It is used for practice, never for mechanism.

### S5. Karltun J, Vogel K, Bergstrand M, Eklund J, "Maintaining knife sharpness in industrial meat cutting: A matter of knife or meat cutter ability", Applied Ergonomics 56: 92-100, 2016 (doi:10.1016/j.apergo.2016.03.010; PMID 27184316)
- Primary: a peer-reviewed quasi-experimental field study of 12 meat cutters at two companies, each using three different knives in normal production. It measured knife cutting force before and after use, rated sharpness and discomfort, and interviewed the cutters. URL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=EXT_ID:27184316%20AND%20SRC:MED&resultType=core&format=json (the PubMed page refused automated access, so nothing was read there)
- Access: read (abstract only, through the Europe PMC record, returned as a paraphrase with short verbatim quotes; the full text is paywalled and was not read)
- Supports: C03, C24. Counterevidence: none found on its finding. A review seen in a search summary notes that studies disagree on whether sharper blades reduce force exposure; that is a lead only. Limits: small sample; professionals in industrial plants, not home cooks; effect sizes and how the instrument was used were not read.
- Status: primary record (abstract). Extending it to home kitchens is our reasoning (M20), not the study's.

### S6. WÜSTHOF, "Frequently Asked Questions", wusthof.com, undated
- Primary (maker), seen only in a search summary. URL: https://wusthof.com/pages/faq
- Access: snippet ("Our sharpening angle for standard blades is 14˚ per side, and for Asian-style blades (Santokus, Nakiris, Chai Daos) is 10˚ per side.")
- Supports: C07 (only the "per side" wording, as a lead). Counterevidence: some WÜSTHOF product pages give 14.5 degrees (snippet).
- Status: lead; not read.

### S7. ZWILLING J.A. Henckels sharpening guidance (a sharpener product page and retailer comparison charts), zwilling.com and williams-sonoma.com, undated
- Primary and retailer material mixed, seen only in a search summary. URLs: https://www.zwilling.com/uk/zwilling-20-cm-abs-v-edge-knife-sharpener-32605-000-0/32605-000-0.html ; https://www.williams-sonoma.com/netstorage/pdf/cutlery-comparison-charts-ZWILLING-final.pdf
- Access: snippet (about 15 degrees per side for European blades, about 10 for Japanese; MIYABI 9-12 degrees per side)
- Supports: C09 (lead only).
- Status: lead; not read.

### S8. Wikipedia, "Honing steel", wikipedia.org, revision not seen
- Popular (encyclopedia). URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honing_steel (the search result linked a mirror)
- Access: snippet (a smooth steel removes no material on a blunt edge and corrects deformation, "burnishing"; studies tend to favour abrasives for daily maintenance)
- Supports: C23 (lead only). Its own sources were not checked.
- Status: lead; not read.

### S9. Science of Sharp, "Carbides in S110V – Part 2/3", scienceofsharp.com, 2022-11-17
- Primary (same author as S1 and S2), seen only in a search summary. URL: https://scienceofsharp.com/2022/11/17/carbides-in-s110v-part-2-3/
- Access: snippet (a carbide pull-through on S110V took nearly 200 microns off the blade height and left cracks and voids among the carbides; stropping on diamond-loaded leather left minimal damage below the surface)
- Supports: T3's material M25 only, as a lead. S110V is a high-carbide powder steel used mostly in pocket knives, not typical of kitchen knives.
- Status: lead; not read.

### S10. McGorry RW, Dowd PC, Dempsey PG, "Cutting moments and grip forces in meat cutting operations and the effect of knife sharpness", Applied Ergonomics 34: 375-382, 2003
- Primary (peer-reviewed), seen only as a citation inside a search summary. URL: none opened.
- Access: snippet (citation only; no abstract seen)
- Supports: C03 (lead only).
- Status: lead; not read.

### S11. CulinaryLore, "Are you really more likely to cut yourself with a dull knife?", culinarylore.com, undated
- Popular (food-writing site), seen only in a search summary. URL: https://culinarylore.com/tools:are-you-really-more-likely-to-cut-yourself-with-a-dull-knife
- Access: snippet (the writer looked for statistics on cuts from dull versus sharp knives and found none)
- Supports: C04 (legend). The other results on this question were forums, a knife retailer's blog and an informal reader poll (snippets).
- Status: lead; not read.

### S12. Search summary of popular whetstone guides (HiConsumption, GearJunkie, Chowhound, Misen, Montana Knife Company, Cook's Illustrated "How to Use a Whetstone"), various dates
- Popular. The summary did not say which site said what. URLs: https://hiconsumption.com/how-to-sharpen-a-knife-with-whetstone/ ; https://gearjunkie.com/how-to-sharpen-knife-whetstone ; https://www.chowhound.com/1939069/how-to-sharpen-a-knife-with-whetstone ; https://misen.com/blogs/news/how-to-use-a-whetstone-the-basics-of-knife-sharpening ; https://www.montanaknifecompany.com/blogs/news/how-to-sharpen-a-knife-with-a-stone ; https://www.americastestkitchen.com/cooksillustrated/articles/275-how-to-use-a-whetstone
- Access: snippet (marker trick; stacked-coin angle guides; "flip the knife and sharpen the other side until the burr transfers back"; "The burr then needs to be removed, otherwise your knife won't cut cleanly"; start at 1000 grit, 200-400 for chips)
- Supports: C06, C10, C18, C20 (leads only). It shows the common account that S1 argues with.
- Status: leads; none read.

### S13. Borough Kitchen, "Whetstones, Steels, Pull-Through Sharpeners: What's Best?", boroughkitchen.com, undated
- Popular (a cookware retailer's blog), seen only in a search summary. URL: https://boroughkitchen.com/blogs/news/which-is-best-for-sharpening-a-knife-whetstones-sharpening-steels-or-pull-through-sharpeners
- Access: snippet (a whetstone is much less abrasive than a pull-through; on a whetstone you are responsible for finding the angle, which takes practice)
- Supports: T3's material M27 only, as a lead.
- Status: lead; not read.

### S14. Science of Sharp, "What is a burr? – part 3", scienceofsharp.com, 2025-07-18
- Primary (same author as S1), seen only in a search summary. URL: https://scienceofsharp.com/2025/07/18/what-is-a-burr-part-3/
- Access: snippet (burr formation begins with deformation near the apex once grinding has made a roughly triangular apex; the conditions for burr formation, and the difference between removing a burr and refining one, are "poorly understood")
- Supports: C12 (lead; the caution in its note).
- Status: lead; not read.
